newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's Jordanian inmates get family visits - ICRC.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's Jordanian inmates get family visits - ICRC.

text.p: Jordanians jailed by Kuwait's state security court after the 1991 Gulf War have received visits by relatives from Amman for the third time, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Wednesday.

"Thirty-four Jordanian citizens imprisoned in Kuwait since after the Gulf War met members of their families between January 6-8, 1997, through an ICRC-organised humanitarian operation," an ICRC statement said.
After Kuwait's Gulf War liberation its courts sentenced dozens of Jordanians, Palestinians and others to long prison terms on charges of assisting Iraqi occupation forces.

"A group of 51 persons, including 17 children, arrived in Kuwait on Monday January 6, 1997. They were assisted by the delegation of the ICRC and met their relatives who are serving long-term sentences issued by the Kuwaiti state security court."
"This was the third family visit organised by the ICRC since the Gulf War," it said. The first two took place in June and September 1995.

"The family visits have been made possible through intensive cooperation and coordination with the ministries of interior and foreign affairs in Kuwait and Jordan and are fully financed by ICRC," it said.
Kuwait's ties with Jordan were strained over its sympathy for Iraq during the seven-month occupation.
